Review Documents Exponential Rise and Cognitive Shift in Judicial Artificial Intelligence

A systematic review and bibliometric study has evaluated a decade of research on artificial intelligence in the judicial domain, documenting an exponential increase in scientific publications between 2015 and 2025. The investigation analyzes how artificial intelligence is reshaping the future of judicial systems, assessing overall scholarly output, international collaborative networks, and evolving theoretical frameworks across the legal field.

To examine this ongoing development, the researchers utilized the PRISMA workflow to screen literature indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection. The screening process encompassed publications appearing between 2015 and 2025, ultimately selecting 610 relevant academic publications for inclusion in the study’s combined bibliometric analysis and systematic review.

The bibliometric findings reveal that research output across the legal technology sector has expanded at an exponential rate throughout the ten-year period. In addition to this surging publication volume, the scientific mapping documents the emergence of an international collaborative network, with global research partnerships centered primarily on institutions in China and the United States.

Scientific mapping of the literature also highlights a fundamental shift in how academic research conceptualizes the role of artificial intelligence within judicial settings. Rather than treating artificial intelligence merely as an efficiency-enhancing tool for routine administrative tasks, scholarly work increasingly views these systems as prospective cognitive partners in complex judicial tasks.

The systematic review indicates that the broader research field has gradually formed a cohesive, three-part knowledge structure. This academic structure is organized around computational techniques, predictive modeling methodologies, and the examination of ethical and governance issues associated with deploying automated intelligence tools in judicial environments.

Despite these substantial research advances, the authors identify three structural challenges that continue to impede progress across the judicial domain. These critical challenges include the ongoing tension between algorithmic explainability and judicial transparency, the persistent impact of data bias, and the uneven distribution of scientific research across the different stages of the judicial process.

To address these unresolved problems, the review emphasizes that future scholarly efforts must foster explainable artificial intelligence systems that align with judicial norms. In addition, the researchers highlight the necessity of establishing full-cycle mechanisms to actively manage data bias, ensuring that bias mitigation is integrated throughout system development and application.

Finally, the authors conclude that future research must strengthen interdisciplinary cooperation between technical and legal communities. Expanding artificial intelligence applications across the entire judicial chain is also essential to resolve procedural imbalances and support the creation of reliable and responsible judicial intelligence.

Subject of Research: Artificial intelligence research trends and structural challenges in the judicial domain

Article Title: Artificial Intelligence in the Judicial Domain: An Integrated Bibliometric and Systematic Review

Article References: Lai, N., Dewi, D. A., Maidin, S. S., Chen, Y., Xiao, W., & Hu, Q. (2026). Artificial Intelligence in the Judicial Domain: An Integrated Bibliometric and Systematic Review. International Journal of Computational Intelligence Systems. https://doi.org/10.1007/s44196-026-01643-y

Keywords: artificial intelligence, judicial system, bibliometric analysis, systematic review, PRISMA workflow, Web of Science, predictive modeling, computational techniques, algorithmic explainability, judicial transparency, data bias, explainable artificial intelligence, judicial intelligence, interdisciplinary cooperation, judicial process, China, United States

News Source: Blake Davidson. (November 20, 2026). Review Documents Exponential Rise and Cognitive Shift in Judicial Artificial Intelligence. Scienmag.
